_about: Controlled vocabulary for the `style` field. Lexical normalisation only — it asserts no facts about what a style is or where it was built (guardrail G2). Canonical labels are the faceting axis (BACKLOG I4, D7); everything after the canonical head belongs in a `styleNote` for display.
_measured: 941 records carried 303 distinct style values, 272 of them appearing exactly once — 93% singletons, so `style` is currently free-text prose rather than a facet. 413 records (44%) carry '—', i.e. no style recorded at all.
_pattern: Most singletons follow `Canonical (qualifier)` or `CanonicalA–CanonicalB fusion`. scripts/normalize-vocab.mjs strips the qualifier into styleNote rather than inventing a new label for each.
_biggest_win: 'Dravidian' (111 records) and 'Dravida' (23) are the same style. Collapsing them is the single largest normalisation gain in the field.

Dravida.note: The corpus uses 'Dravidian' and 'Dravida' interchangeably; 'Dravida' is the term used in the silpa texts.
